To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tumor suppressor p53, p53 family members p73 and p63, regulate the miRNA-processing components, such as Dicer, Drosha, DGCR8, and Argonautes.
p53, p53, and p63 appear to regulate the components of miRNA processing complex, such as Dicer, Drosha, and TRBP2.
the tumor suppressor genes p53, p53, and p63 function as both positive as well as negative regulators of the major miRNA processing complex, and they regulate the processing of a number of miRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the p53-miRNAs that regulate components of miRNA processing machinery and how they regulate tumorigenesis.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the components of miRNA processing complex and how they regulate the miRNA expression.
the regulation of the miRNA biogenesis complex by p53, p53 family members, and their target miRNAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53/p63 and p73 are positive and negative regulators for the miRNA processing.
p63/p73 and p53 regulate the components of miRNA processing machinery and the miRNAs that target the processing machinery.
p53, p53, and p63 function as positive and negative regulators for a number of components involved in the miRNA processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p53, p53, and p73 are regulators of the miRNAs that target the miRNA processing and they regulate the components of miRNA processing machinery.
p53/p63 regulate the components of miRNA processing machinery and the miRNAs, which regulate the components of this machinery.
the tumor suppressor p53, p53-related proteins p63 and p73, and miRNAs are the regulators of the components of the RNAi processing machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miRNA processing complex is regulated by the tumor suppressors, p53, p53, and p73.
the tumor suppressor proteins p53, p53, and p63 function as both positive as well as negative regulators of the components of the processing complex.
the tumor suppressor proteins p53, p53, and p63 regulate the miRNA-processing machinery, which in turn regulates the processing and expression of miRNAs.
